outcome: One operator set in every authoring language: // and % everywhere, and and/or/not in Initialization
owner_impact: First release of #577 (one code grammar). Every code artifact now has the same operators. Controller, Metrics and the environment field gain // (floor division) and % (remainder, whose sign follows the divisor as in Python), computed identically in the simulator and in Initialization. Initialization gains and/or/not. As in the Controller and Metrics, both sides of and/or are always evaluated, so random draws never depend on the other side's value. Nothing that worked before changes: the 28,059-case check shows that the only programs whose result changed are ones that were rejected before because they used one of these operators, and the simulator's reference runs are bit-identical. The grammar contract GPT reads is now vlab.authoring/0.10, stating these operators and rules, and the MCP is redeployed with it. Test now: optional. In a Controller, try something like `phase = (step_count // 10) % 2` with a scalar, or `if a and not b:` in Initialization.

next.text: #577 release 2: loops over a fixed number range, `for k in range(K)` with a constant K, in the Controller and Metrics. It has not started yet.

technical_evidence: Rust: crates/kernel/src/scalar_ops.rs (floor_divide, modulo); controller, metrics and environment IR accept // and %; new Rust tests; the 5 reference runs are bit-identical natively and on WebAssembly.

JS: the typed grammar (Controller, Metrics) and the environment field gain // and %, scalar-only in the type rules; Initialization gains and/or/not with boolean operands and eager evaluation. New authoring-operators.test.mjs (6 tests).
Equivalence: 54 of 28,059 cases changed, every one containing one of the new operators or keywords; each was classified old versus new before the golden file was regenerated.

Contract vlab.authoring/0.10 adds code_grammar and per-artifact arithmetic operators; MCP server 3.19.0. The database stores the version as text with no value check. 699 tests pass; full browser smoke passes.
